experiences.name: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike
experiences.description: Walk the iconic shoreline trail around the turquoise glacial waters of Lake Louise, with stunning views of the Victoria Glacier. Extend the hike to the Plain of Six Glaciers teahouse for panoramic alpine scenery. One of the most photographed lakes in the world and a must-do for nature lovers.
experiences.location: Lake Louise Village, Banff National Park

experiences.name: Moraine Lake & Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek
experiences.description: Hike the Rockpile Trail and Lakeshore Trail at Moraine Lake, surrounded by the dramatic Valley of the Ten Peaks. The vivid blue water is fed by glacial meltwater and is arguably even more stunning than Lake Louise. Reserve a shuttle in advance as private vehicles are restricted during peak season.
experiences.location: Moraine Lake Road, Banff National Park

experiences.name: Sulphur Mountain Gondola & Summit Boardwalk
experiences.description: Ride the Banff Gondola to the summit of Sulphur Mountain at 2,281 metres for breathtaking 360-degree views of six mountain ranges. Walk the 1 km summit boardwalk to Sanson Peak weather observatory. Alternatively, hike up the Sulphur Mountain Trail to save on gondola costs and earn the views.

experiences.name: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike
experiences.description: Follow the catwalk trail carved into the limestone canyon walls to reach the Lower and Upper Falls of Johnston Canyon. Continue further to the Ink Pots, a series of colourful cold-water springs set in an open meadow. This moderate hike offers dramatic canyon scenery, wildlife spotting, and lush forest immersion.

experiences.name: Canoe Rental on Vermilion Lakes
experiences.description: Paddle a canoe across the serene Vermilion Lakes at golden hour, with Mount Rundle reflecting perfectly in the still water. This area is one of the best wildlife corridors in Banff, offering excellent chances to spot elk, beavers, herons, and eagles. A peaceful and deeply immersive nature experience just minutes from Banff Townsite.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary Airport at 14:00. Take the Banff Airporter shuttle (~$60 CAD one-way, budget-friendly shared service) to Banff town (~1.5 hrs). Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge. Drop off luggage and take a leisurely stroll along Banff Avenue to get oriented with the town.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Banff town centre on foot. Walk down to the Bow River and enjoy the free views of Bow Falls and the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel from the public lookout. Watch the golden hour light on the surrounding peaks — completely free and spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the Calgary Airport food court before departure, or pick up groceries at Safeway in Banff (~$10–15 CAD) once you arrive to stock up for the week
meals.dinner: Nourish Bistro on Bear Street — plant-forward, generous portions, budget-friendly mains around $15–20 CAD. Great for a low-key first night.

day_by_day.notes: Stop at the Safeway or IGA grocery store in Banff on your first evening to stock up on snacks, trail mix, sandwiches, and water bottles for hikes — this will save significant money throughout the trip. Pick up a Banff National Park day pass or confirm your Parks Canada Discovery Pass ($72.25 CAD/person annual pass is excellent value if you plan multiple park visits).

day_by_day.morning: Early start — take the Roam Transit Bus Route 8X from Banff to Lake Louise (departs ~7:30 AM, ~$10 CAD each way). Arrive at Lake Louise and begin the Lake Louise Shoreline Hike. Walk the iconic turquoise glacial shoreline trail, heading from the Chateau Lake Louise to the far end of the lake and back (~4 km round trip, easy, 1–1.5 hrs). Stunning views of Victoria Glacier. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the shoreline walk, take the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail extension if energy allows (adds ~8 km round trip from the lake, moderate difficulty) for dramatic glacier views and a teahouse stop. Alternatively, relax on the lakeshore, have your packed lunch, and take photos. Return to Banff via Roam Transit Bus in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at the lodge. Take a short evening walk to Tunnel Mountain Trailhead viewpoint (15-minute walk from town) for panoramic sunset views over the Bow Valley — free and easily accessible.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared breakfast using groceries from Safeway (oatmeal, fruit, coffee) at the lodge — ~$3–5 CAD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from grocery store: sandwiches, trail mix, granola bars, and a reusable water bottle filled at the lodge — ~$5–8 CAD
meals.dinner: Tooloulou's Restaurant in Banff — casual Cajun-inspired menu with affordable options around $15–22 CAD. Try the wraps or pasta dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Roam Transit is the most budget-friendly way to reach Lake Louise. Buy a multi-day Roam pass if available to save money across the trip. Bring layers — even at 25°C in town, the lakeshore can be breezy and cool in the morning. Arrive at Lake Louise before 8 AM to secure a spot on the bus and avoid peak crowds at the lake.

day_by_day.morning: Take Roam Transit Route 10 to Moraine Lake (mandatory — private vehicles are restricted, bus departs early from Lake Louise Village, connect via Route 8X from Banff). Arrive at Moraine Lake and hike the Rockpile Trail first (20-minute scramble, easy-moderate) for the iconic Valley of the Ten Peaks panorama — one of the most photographed views in Canada. Then begin the Lakeshore Trail (~3.4 km round trip, easy) along the brilliant blue-green lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Moraine Lake area. Bring a packed lunch and eat on the lakeshore with the Ten Peaks as your backdrop. If time and energy allow, extend the hike toward Consolation Lakes (~6 km round trip from Moraine Lake, moderate) for a quieter, equally stunning alternative trail. Return to Banff via Roam Transit by mid-to-late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the lodge. Walk to the free Banff Visitor Centre to pick up trail maps and learn about the park's wildlife and geology. Enjoy a quiet evening stroll along the Bow River Pathway.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at lodge — instant oatmeal, banana, instant coffee — ~$3–5 CAD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch: wraps, cheese, apple, energy bars from grocery store — ~$6–8 CAD. Eat at the Moraine Lake lakeshore.
meals.dinner: Banff Ave Brewing Co. — casual pub atmosphere with affordable burgers, flatbreads, and mains around $18–24 CAD. Happy hour deals often available.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake road is closed to private vehicles — Roam Transit is the only public option and books up fast. Book your Roam Transit seats in advance online (roamtransit.com). Depart Banff very early (6:30–7:00 AM bus) to maximize time at Moraine Lake before it gets crowded. This is the most popular day of the itinerary — plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike — take Roam Transit Route 1 from Banff toward Canmore and get off at Johnston Canyon stop (~20 min, ~$5 CAD). Begin the catwalk trail carved into the limestone canyon walls. Hike to the Lower Falls (~1.1 km one way, easy, 30 mins) and continue to the Upper Falls (~2.7 km one way from trailhead, easy-moderate, ~1.5 hrs total). The canyon walls, rushing water, and spray are spectacular on a warm summer day.
day_by_day.afternoon: For the adventurous, continue beyond the Upper Falls to the Ink Pots — seven cold-water mineral springs in a beautiful open meadow (~5.8 km one way from trailhead, moderate). This makes for a full and rewarding half-day hike. Return to Banff via Roam Transit in the afternoon. Stop at the Banff Farmers Market (if running on Wednesdays) or browse the town.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Banff townsite. Walk up to the Banff Centre Hill for free panoramic views of the valley. Watch the sunset over the Rockies from the free public viewpoint on Tunnel Mountain Drive.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at lodge — toast, peanut butter, banana, coffee — ~$3–4 CAD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Ink Pots or Upper Falls area — sandwiches, trail mix, fruit — ~$6–8 CAD
meals.dinner: The Elk & Oarsman pub on Banff Avenue — affordable pub fare, burgers and nachos around $15–20 CAD, lively atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon is one of the most accessible and rewarding hikes near Banff town. The catwalk sections can be slippery from waterfall mist — wear good grip hiking shoes. The Ink Pots extension adds significant distance but is highly recommended on a clear warm day. Bring a light rain jacket as the canyon spray can be refreshing but wetting.

day_by_day.morning: Hike Tunnel Mountain Trail — a classic, free, and easily accessible hike right from Banff townsite (no transit needed). Trailhead is a 10-minute walk from the lodge. The hike is ~4.8 km round trip, moderate, and takes about 1.5–2 hours. Summit offers 360-degree views of the Bow Valley, Banff town, Cascade Mountain, and the Fairmont Banff Springs. A perfect budget-friendly morning with zero transport cost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Banff Legacy Trail or rent a bike from Soul Ski & Bike (~$30–40 CAD for a half day) and cycle the paved Bow Valley Parkway trail section for stunning mountain and river scenery. Alternatively, visit the free Banff Park Museum (National Historic Site, ~$4 CAD entry) on Banff Avenue — a fascinating Victorian-era natural history museum with taxidermied wildlife displays.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a soak at Banff Upper Hot Springs (~$16.50 CAD adult entry) — a well-earned reward after days of hiking. The outdoor mineral pool with mountain views is a Banff institution and very affordable. Return to town for a final evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at lodge — yogurt, granola, fruit — ~$4–5 CAD
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the summit of Tunnel Mountain or along the Bow Valley Parkway — packed from grocery store — ~$6–8 CAD
meals.dinner: Coyotes Southwestern Grill on Caribou Street — fresh, flavourful Southwestern cuisine with mains around $18–25 CAD. Excellent value and quality.

day_by_day.notes: Tunnel Mountain is an ideal rest-day hike — shorter and less strenuous than previous days, giving your legs some recovery while still offering spectacular views. The Banff Upper Hot Springs are open daily and are a quintessential Banff experience. Bring a towel or rent one at the springs for a small fee (~$2 CAD). Book the hot springs visit for early evening (6–7 PM) to catch the alpenglow on the surrounding peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning walk along the Bow River Trail from town — a flat, easy, and free 2–3 km riverside walk through forest and meadow with excellent wildlife spotting opportunities (elk, deer, ground squirrels are common). Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge. Store luggage at the lodge if needed while you enjoy your last few hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your final afternoon exploring any missed spots in Banff town: browse the shops on Banff Avenue, visit the free Cascade Gardens behind the Parks Canada Administration Building, or grab a final coffee at a local café. Book the Banff Airporter shuttle back to Calgary Airport for your departure flight — book in advance to secure your seat.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Banff for Calgary Airport via Banff Airporter shuttle. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the shuttle ride and airport check-in.

meals.breakfast: Wild Flour Bakery on Bear Street — excellent fresh-baked pastries, muffins, and coffee for ~$8–12 CAD. A wonderful final Banff breakfast treat.
meals.lunch: Grab a final affordable meal at Subway or pick up a wrap from the Safeway deli counter before heading to the shuttle — ~$8–12 CAD
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Calgary Airport or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11 AM — confirm with Banff Mountain Lodge. Book your return Banff Airporter shuttle well in advance as summer seats fill up quickly. Use any remaining grocery store snacks and packed food for the shuttle ride to the airport. Take one last look at the Rockies as you depart — a fitting farewell to a spectacular budget adventure in Banff National Park.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:00. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary International Airport at 14:00. Collect luggage and take the Banff Airporter shuttle (~1.5 hours) to Banff town. Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge, freshen up, and take a leisurely self-guided walk along Banff Avenue to get oriented — browse local shops and enjoy the mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Canoe Rental on Vermilion Lakes: Head to Vermilion Lakes (just 10 minutes from Banff town centre) for a golden-hour canoe paddle as the sun sets behind Mount Rundle. A perfect, low-effort introduction to Banff's natural beauty after a travel day.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or at Calgary Airport before boarding the shuttle.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or pack snacks for the shuttle ride.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bison Restaurant & Terrace in Banff town — locally sourced Canadian cuisine with a warm mountain atmosphere. Mid-range pricing, around $35–55 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Banff Airporter shuttle in advance online. Canoe rentals at Vermilion Lakes are available through local outfitters like Banff Adventures — book ahead for a sunset slot. Carry a light jacket for the evening on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike: Drive or take the Roam Transit bus (~45 minutes from Banff) to Lake Louise. Walk the iconic shoreline trail around the turquoise glacial waters, taking in stunning views of the Victoria Glacier and surrounding peaks. The trail is easy and approximately 4 km return — perfect for a refreshing morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the shoreline walk, explore the Lake Louise area further. Visit the historic Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise for a coffee or afternoon tea on the lakeside terrace, or rent a canoe directly on Lake Louise for an hour of paddling on the glacial water. Return to Banff by mid-afternoon for some rest.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Banff town centre. Visit the Banff Park Museum National Historic Site or browse the local galleries. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Whitebark Cafe in Banff — great coffee and baked goods to fuel the morning hike.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Lake Louise — pick up sandwiches and snacks from Laggan's Mountain Bakery & Deli at the Lake Louise village mall. Eat with a view of the lake.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Saltlik Steakhouse in Banff — known for Alberta beef and a lively atmosphere. Expect $40–60 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Lake Louise early (before 9:00 AM) to secure parking or take the Roam Transit Bus 8X for a stress-free and eco-friendly option. Lake Louise can get very busy by mid-morning in July. Sunscreen and water are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake & Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek: Take the Parks Canada shuttle or a pre-booked tour bus from Lake Louise to Moraine Lake (private vehicles are restricted in peak season). Hike the Rockpile Trail (20 minutes, iconic viewpoint) and then continue along the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return) surrounded by the dramatic Valley of the Ten Peaks. One of the most photographed landscapes in Canada.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff by early afternoon. Relax at the hotel or take a gentle walk along the Bow River Trail near Banff town — flat, scenic, and ideal for unwinding after a big morning hike.
day_by_day.evening: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike (evening option): Drive or take a taxi to Johnston Canyon (~25 minutes from Banff). Walk the catwalk trail carved into the limestone canyon walls to reach the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km return from trailhead). The canyon is beautifully lit in the evening and far less crowded than midday.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel — aim to leave for Moraine Lake by 7:30 AM to catch the shuttle.
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch for Moraine Lake — there are no mid-range dining options there. Bring a reusable water bottle and trail snacks.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Coyotes Southwestern Grill in Banff — fresh, flavourful Southwestern-inspired dishes in a casual setting. Around $25–40 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake Road is closed to private vehicles in 2027 — book the Parks Canada shuttle or a guided tour well in advance as spots sell out weeks ahead. Wear sturdy hiking shoes. Johnston Canyon in the evening is magical — bring a headlamp for the return walk if staying past dusk.

day_by_day.morning: Sulphur Mountain Gondola & Summit Boardwalk: Take the Banff Gondola (just 5 minutes from the town centre) to the summit of Sulphur Mountain at 2,281 metres. Walk the 1 km summit boardwalk connecting to Sanson Peak, enjoying breathtaking 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the summit interpretive centre and viewpoints.
day_by_day.afternoon: After descending from Sulphur Mountain, visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs — located at the base of the gondola — for a relaxing soak in the thermal mineral waters with mountain views. A perfect mid-range treat after the morning's activity.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Cave and Basin National Historic Site (open until 5:00 PM — adjust if needed) or take a peaceful walk along the Sundance Canyon Trail near the Bow River. Enjoy a relaxed evening in Banff town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Evelyn's Coffee Bar in Banff — cozy and popular with locals.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Sky Bistro at the top of the Sulphur Mountain Gondola — panoramic views with a mid-range menu. Expect $25–40 CAD per person. Reserve a table when booking gondola tickets.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Banff Ave Brewing Co. — craft beers brewed on-site with a solid pub-style menu in a fun, social atmosphere. Around $25–40 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Banff Gondola tickets online in advance to avoid queues — combo tickets with Sky Bistro are available. The Banff Upper Hot Springs requires a separate admission (~$16 CAD per person). Bring a swimsuit and towel for the hot springs.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike (morning alternative if not done on Day 3, or substitute with Ink Pots hike extension): If you visited Johnston Canyon in the evening on Day 3, use this morning for a longer hike — extend the Johnston Canyon trail beyond the Upper Falls to the Ink Pots (11.6 km return), a series of colourful natural springs in a stunning open meadow. Alternatively, explore the Tunnel Mountain Trail from Banff town (4.8 km loop, 1.5 hours) for great views without driving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff for a leisurely afternoon. Visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies to learn about the history and culture of the Rockies, or browse Banff's independent shops along Banff Avenue for souvenirs and local goods.
day_by_day.evening: Canoe Rental on Vermilion Lakes (second visit at golden hour, or first visit if Day 1 was too tired): Return to Vermilion Lakes for another serene paddle at sunset — the lighting and reflections are extraordinary in July. A wonderful way to wind down before the final full day.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Wild Flour Bakery in Banff — artisan breads, pastries, and excellent coffee. A local favourite.
meals.lunch: Picnic at the Ink Pots meadow (pack from town) or grab lunch at Trailhead Cafe near Johnston Canyon.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Maple Leaf Restaurant in Banff — Canadian cuisine with a focus on local ingredients like Alberta bison, elk, and fresh fish. Around $40–60 CAD per person. A great splurge night.

day_by_day.notes: If extending to the Ink Pots, allow 4–5 hours for the full return hike. Wear layers as the meadow can be cooler and windier. Vermilion Lakes canoe rentals should be booked in advance for a specific sunset time slot.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning hike or scenic drive along the Bow Valley Parkway (Highway 1A) — a quieter, wildlife-rich alternative to the Trans-Canada Highway. Stop at Castle Mountain viewpoint and Silverton Falls trailhead (1.6 km return, easy). Watch for elk, deer, and bighorn sheep along the roadside. Return to Banff by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge. Pack bags and store luggage at the hotel if needed. Spend final hours in Banff town — last-minute shopping, a coffee on the terrace, or a walk along the Bow River. Board the Banff Airporter shuttle back to Calgary International Airport (allow 2.5–3 hours before departure including check-in time).
day_by_day.evening: Travel home. Depart from Calgary International Airport.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast in Banff at Melissa's Missteak — a Banff institution serving hearty breakfasts since 1972. Great value and a classic way to end the trip.
meals.lunch: Light lunch or snack at a Banff Avenue cafe before heading to the shuttle, or grab food at Calgary Airport.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Calgary International Airport or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Check shuttle schedules carefully based on your flight departure time — book the return Banff Airporter in advance. Hotel checkout is typically 11:00 AM; ask the lodge about late checkout or luggage storage. Leave time for wildlife spotting on the Bow Valley Parkway — it is best enjoyed slowly and without a tight schedule.

Visit the historic Cosmic Ray Station, a National Historic Site at the summit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike: Drive approximately 25 minutes northwest along the Bow Valley Parkway to Johnston Canyon. Walk the dramatic catwalk trail carved into the limestone canyon walls to reach the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km). For the adventurous, continue to the Ink Pots — vivid cold-water springs another 3 km beyond. Total round-trip approximately 2–3 hours at a leisurely premium pace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff for a relaxing evening. Enjoy cocktails at the lodge's bar or lounge, then head out for a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the lodge — opt for the full Canadian breakfast featuring eggs Benedict with smoked Alberta trout, fresh fruit, and artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch prepared by the lodge's kitchen and packed in a premium hamper — enjoy it trailside at Johnston Canyon's Upper Falls viewing platform.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eden Restaurant at the Rimrock Resort Hotel — Banff's only AAA Four Diamond restaurant, offering an exceptional tasting menu with wine pairings, featuring locally sourced Alberta ingredients with French-inspired technique and stunning mountain views.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Banff Gondola tickets online in advance to avoid queues. The gondola opens at 8:00 AM. Johnston Canyon can get busy by mid-morning; arriving after lunch helps avoid peak crowds. Wear sturdy hiking shoes for both activities.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake & Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek: Depart early (private vehicle or lodge-arranged shuttle recommended, as the Moraine Lake Road requires a reservation or shuttle pass). Hike the Rockpile Trail (short but steep, 300 m) to the iconic viewpoint overlooking Moraine Lake and the Valley of the Ten Peaks — arguably the most photographed scene in Canada. Then descend and walk the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return) along the vivid turquoise shoreline for up-close views of the glacial lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike: Continue to nearby Lake Louise (approximately 15 minutes from Moraine Lake). Walk the iconic shoreline trail around the brilliant emerald glacial waters with the Victoria Glacier as your backdrop. The trail (4 km return) is flat and accessible, allowing you to soak in the extraordinary scenery at a leisurely pace. Stop at the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise for afternoon tea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff for a well-earned rest, spa session at the lodge, or a soak in the Banff Upper Hot Springs.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before 7:00 AM departure — continental spread with fresh pastries, yogurt parfaits, and specialty coffee to fuel the day.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise's Lakeview Lounge — enjoy elevated comfort food (gourmet burgers, wild mushroom soup, smoked salmon plates) with unobstructed views directly over Lake Louise.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Juniper Bistro at The Juniper Hotel — a locally beloved restaurant with a stunning open terrace overlooking the Bow Valley, serving modern Canadian cuisine with an emphasis on wild game, foraged herbs, and regional produce.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake Road requires advance reservations for private vehicles or use of the Parks Canada shuttle system — book months in advance as spots sell out quickly. Arrive at Moraine Lake before 8:00 AM for the best light and fewest crowds. Bring layers as mornings at altitude are cool (10–15°C). This is a full and rewarding day — wear comfortable hiking boots.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at Banff Mountain Lodge. Sleep in, enjoy a luxurious breakfast, and take advantage of the lodge's spa or wellness facilities. Alternatively, take a peaceful morning walk along the Bow River Trail (flat, scenic, 5 km loop) directly accessible from central Banff — ideal for wildlife spotting including elk and beavers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Canoe Rental on Vermilion Lakes (second visit, different time of day): Return to the Vermilion Lakes for an afternoon paddle to experience the lakes in a different light. Explore the wetland channels and birdwatch for great blue herons, ospreys, and bald eagles. Alternatively, arrange a guided fly-fishing excursion on the Bow River through the lodge's concierge for a premium angling experience.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Banff Avenue boutiques and galleries at your leisure. Pick up premium Canadian souvenirs, Indigenous art, or outdoor gear from Banff's high-end shops.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent late breakfast at the lodge — eggs your way, smoked salmon bagels, house-made granola, and fresh-pressed juices.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Saltlik Steakhouse in downtown Banff — a premium steakhouse known for its Alberta AAA beef, fresh seafood tower, and craft cocktails in a sophisticated atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Chez François — an intimate French-Canadian bistro in Banff offering classic escargot, duck confit, and an exceptional cheese board, with a curated Burgundy and Bordeaux wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Day 4 is intentionally lighter to allow recovery from the demanding Day 3 hikes. This is a great day to book a spa treatment at the lodge or a guided Bow River float trip. The afternoon canoe session on Vermilion Lakes is equally beautiful in afternoon light as at golden hour.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive — optional full-day premium excursion: Hire a private guide and luxury vehicle for a curated drive along the Icefields Parkway (Highway 93), one of the world's most scenic roads. Stop at Bow Lake, Peyto Lake viewpoint (a vivid wolf-shaped turquoise lake), and the Columbia Icefield. Board the Ice Explorer for a guided glacier walk on the Athabasca Glacier — a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Icefields Parkway to the Glacier Skywalk — a glass-floored observation platform suspended 280 metres above the Sunwapta Valley. Enjoy the dramatic views before beginning the scenic return drive to Banff, stopping at Sunwapta Falls and Athabasca Falls along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by early evening. Relax at the lodge with a private in-room dining experience or a sunset cocktail on your suite's balcony overlooking the mountains.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before 7:30 AM departure for the Icefields Parkway.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic hamper prepared by the lodge and enjoyed at Peyto Lake or Bow Lake — premium charcuterie, artisan cheese, smoked meats, fresh fruit, and sparkling water amid breathtaking scenery.
meals.dinner: Private in-suite dining at Banff Mountain Lodge — arrange a curated tasting menu delivered to your suite with a sommelier-selected wine pairing for an intimate, luxurious end to an extraordinary day.

day_by_day.notes: The Icefields Parkway day trip is approximately 450 km return and takes a full day. Book a private luxury vehicle and licensed guide through the lodge concierge well in advance. Bring warm layers — the Columbia Icefield is significantly colder (near 0°C) even in summer. The Ice Explorer glacier walk and Glacier Skywalk require advance tickets.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning hike — Johnston Canyon revisit or Tunnel Mountain Trail: For a lighter farewell hike, ascend Tunnel Mountain (2.5 km one way, moderate) directly from Banff townsite for panoramic views over the Bow Valley, the Fairholme Range, and the hoodoos below. The summit is reached in about 45 minutes and offers one of the best accessible viewpoints near town — perfect for final photos and reflection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge after a leisurely late checkout (arrange with concierge). Enjoy a final stroll through Banff, browse the Cave and Basin National Historic Site (birthplace of Canada's national park system), and collect any last souvenirs before your private transfer to Calgary International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Banff via private luxury transfer to Calgary International Airport. Reflect on an extraordinary week in the Canadian Rockies.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at the lodge — indulge in the full premium spread one last time: eggs Benedict, smoked Alberta trout, fresh pastries, fruit platters, and specialty lattes.
meals.lunch: Final lunch at The Bison Restaurant and Terrace in Banff — a farm-to-table gem celebrating Alberta's finest ingredients with dishes like bison short rib, wild mushroom risotto, and house-made charcuterie on a charming outdoor terrace.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Calgary Airport Maple Leaf Lounge or at a restaurant near the airport if time permits before your departure flight.

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout (1:00–2:00 PM) from the lodge concierge in advance. The transfer from Banff to Calgary Airport takes approximately 1.5 hours — allow at least 3 hours before your flight. The Cave and Basin National Historic Site is a 10-minute walk from downtown Banff and is a worthwhile final stop. Ensure all Parks Canada passes and activity receipts are collected for memories.
